title: Milestone closed, one of its own issues never did
author: off-by-one
description: Compares a repository's own milestones against its own issues: a milestone reads state=closed, but an issue still assigned to it reads state=open. Unlike merged-pr-issue-still-open/issue-closed-pr-still-open (a PR's own closing-keyword promise) or duplicate-issue-still-open (a prose 'duplicate of #N' marker), a milestone carries no auto-close wiring to any of its issues at all -- closing a milestone on GitHub never touches the state of a single issue inside it. The seam exists only by holding the milestone record and its issue's record at the same instant; neither alone shows it.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the milestone has been closed while one of its own issues sits open, not flat. Under 24 hours since the milestone closed scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- whoever closed the milestone may not have swept its issues within a day). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal: a milestone that reads closed while one of its own issues reads open. The 24h window matches merged-pr-issue-still-open's and duplicate-issue-still-open's own bar (a clear, easily-verified resolution signal), not contributor-thanked-not-credited's slower 72h (crediting a README is a deliberate edit, not a one-click follow-up). An issue that is itself already closed, carries no milestone at all, or is assigned to a milestone that is itself still open is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the identical discipline every recipe before this one holds.
